content.text: The atlas tools were denied, so I'll fall back to normal search.

Changing the props of `TelegramLinkWidget` (`app/portal/components/TelegramLinkWidget.tsx`) affects two pages:

| Page | Route | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `app/portal/supplier/page.tsx:715` | `/portal/supplier` | `<TelegramLinkWidget role="supplier" />` |
| `app/portal/reseller/page.tsx:741` | `/portal/reseller` | `<TelegramLinkWidget role="reseller" />` |

Both pages pass only `role`. Any new required prop, or a change to the type of `role`, would break both call sites.

The test `test/portal-telegram-widget.test.ts` also builds the component with `{ role: "reseller" }` and `{ role: "supplier" }`. It would need updating too.

I couldn't use the atlas tools (`fullstack_impact` and `fullstack_component`) because permission was denied, so I used a text search. It found every reference to the component, so no other pages import it. The component calls three API routes: `/api/v2/auth/telegram/status`, `/link-token` and `/unlink`. Those only matter if your change touches what it fetches, not just its props.
